nodes.label: Myrosta Council Review
nodes.rationale: Seven review lenses, 81 findings, 18 code claims adversarially verified (17 confirmed); goal frame: best flexible rostering for healthcare.

nodes.label: Department Board Spec v2
nodes.rationale: v2 supersedes v1: single-row-per-hospital schema could not stop one group overwriting another because Postgres RLS is row-level; v1 also shipped no RLS and a false determinism claim.

nodes.label: Department Configuration
nodes.rationale: Zones, min/max cover, extra-slot unlock order, self-roster method, fixed patterns with Any (auto) zone, quota period - all per-cycle.

nodes.label: Self-Roster Round
nodes.rationale: Auto-draft the base roster, release for self-roster, watch coverage fill live, optionally schedule auto-open/close with countdown and notifications.

nodes.label: Collision-Proof Booking
nodes.rationale: Impossible to double-book: a taken slot disappears for everyone else and only one simultaneous booking sticks.

nodes.label: Passwordless OTP Sign-In
nodes.rationale: No passwords: 6-digit SMS or email code, then the device stays signed in; shared-computer mode signs out on close/idle.

nodes.label: My Shifts
nodes.rationale: Own shifts as list or month calendar, Add to calendar push with reminders, pink L for locum shifts.

nodes.label: Self-Roster Methods
nodes.rationale: Cohort waves, snake-draft, guarded booking, auto-draft + adjust - fairness rules and quotas mean the last to log in still gets a fair go.

nodes.label: Deterministic Rules Engine
nodes.rationale: Instant, free, reproducible vs LLM per-run cost; governance line: no external AI processes staff data (IRIS pipes workforce data through Claude/GPT). Steal only the narration idea, generated deterministically.

nodes.label: IRIS
nodes.rationale: Emergency-medicine-first AI-generation rostering platform; positioning word-for-word Myrosta's, validating the market thesis while contesting the differentiation claim.

nodes.label: Configurable Fatigue Rules
nodes.rationale: Min break / max consecutive days / no clinical after on-call as canBook warn-or-block with admin override; clinical safety, procurement checkbox, junior-doctor market gate.

nodes.label: Configuration Presets
nodes.rationale: 3-4 named presets with raw controls behind Advanced prevent the per-cycle config matrix from killing zero-training onboarding at org #3-5.

nodes.label: DST Week-Math Bug
nodes.rationale: Math.floor over ms difference flips fortnight A/B parity after the 4 Oct 2026 spring-forward; must be fixed before the 28 Sep cycle is prepared.

nodes.label: Entra ID SSO
nodes.rationale: Australian health services require Entra ID SSO for staff-facing apps; must land inside the multi-org milestone - retrofitting after tenants onboard is far costlier.

nodes.label: Equity Analytics View
nodes.rationale: Renders over existing assign data, no schema change; simultaneously pilot trust-builder, director's adoption justification, and the moat's evidence layer.

nodes.label: FACEM Distribution Channel
nodes.rationale: Clinician-founder who rosters with his own product, selling director-to-director through the college network - a channel vendors cannot authentically access.

nodes.label: Hardcoded Two-Period Day
nodes.rationale: AM/PM-only day model is the single biggest blocker to best-flexible-rostering: walls off every market beyond consultant groups.

nodes.label: Pilot Conversion
nodes.rationale: The single event everything depends on: if the 3 Aug-27 Sep parallel-run ends with Excel staying authoritative, every downstream investment is wasted. Agree written criteria with the ED director.

nodes.label: RLS Org-Blob Delete Exposure
nodes.rationale: Any allow-listed member can rewrite or delete the whole org blob; admin role exists only in client JS. Acceptable for the pilot, procurement blocker for hospital #2 - server-side write authority rides with the multi-org milestone.

nodes.label: RosterOn Payroll Bridge
nodes.rationale: Be the roster of record and bridge to incumbent payroll, never calculate pay; the export is the strongest retire-Excel argument.

nodes.label: Self-Rostering Fairness Engine
nodes.rationale: Four modes (guarded free-for-all, snake, cohort waves, auto-draft+adjust) with per-fortnight quotas; incumbents are architecturally and culturally unable to ship it quickly.

nodes.label: Sync Hardening Session
nodes.rationale: Union-by-id merges, per-key 3-way assign reconcile with tombstones, post-merge invariant pass, merge-not-replace realtime; ~5 functions, do before the pilot opens 3 Aug.

nodes.label: Sync-Layer Silent Data Loss Family
nodes.rationale: Six distinct silent-loss modes (mine-wins arrays, resurrections, unvalidated merged bookings) share one root cause; exactly the trust-destroying failures that would kill pilot conversion.

nodes.label: Whole-Blob CAS Merge Architecture
nodes.rationale: Defensible for one ~30-person org for 12 months; three planned ceilings: truly 3-way merge semantics, egress/realtime fanout cost, relational rows at nursing/JMO scale.

nodes.label: Best-Engine Build Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Post-cutover order: department board (site-2 wow), nights behind a per-org flag, preference-week draw engine, scribe shadow-roster, add-group wizard, credential gating.

nodes.label: Cutover Readiness Gates
nodes.rationale: Nothing runs before its gate: pilot ended, trademark filed, migration rehearsed twice on a restored clone, engine tests green, rollback verified runnable.

nodes.label: Production Cutover Window
nodes.rationale: ~45-min ordered window; order is load-bearing (old app must never run against new schema); abort at any red 1.9-1.12 via rollback, which is policies-only since no roster data moves.

nodes.label: Board Slice Schema
nodes.rationale: One row per (hospital, org) so row-level security genuinely isolates each group's digest; removes shared-row merge and CAS contention; never reuses the roster's CAS token.

nodes.label: Department Board
nodes.rationale: One screen of who is on now across every staff group - turns five rosters into one department; each group publishes a small digest, everyone in the hospital reads all digests; names only, never pay/leave reasons.

nodes.label: Deterministic Slice Build
nodes.rationale: Two synced devices must emit identical bytes or the publish gate loops; buildSlice takes the cycle as argument, avoids per-device state, sorts entries and hash-gates the write.

nodes.label: Hospitals Registry
nodes.rationale: Free-text hospital strings split one department into two boards or merge unrelated sites on a typo (cross-hospital disclosure); id registry + FK with server-derived identity fixes it.

nodes.label: Capacity Check
nodes.rationale: Pre-release sanity: cover x zones x 7 days vs what the group can staff.

nodes.label: Staff Group
nodes.rationale: The hospital decides which groups it has - no fixed catalogue; a group = its own roster, staff list and fairness; ~30 minutes setup from the same engine baseline.

nodes.label: Ten Setup Questions
nodes.rationale: Name, role noun, zones, cover min-max, shift times, cycle length, quota counting, self-roster method, fatigue rules, feature switches.

nodes.label: Admin-Composed Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Four modes deployed by the admin per grade, per cycle, per stage - control never leaves them; shipped as named presets to guard against the configuration wall.

nodes.label: Choice Within Duty
nodes.rationale: Constrained self-rostering for juniors: you cannot choose whether you do your share of nights and weekends - you choose which ones. No Australian hospital offers juniors self-rostering.

nodes.label: EBA Rule Packs
nodes.rationale: Hard floors encoded per enterprise agreement with HR sign-off - roster legality only, never pay interpretation; pack #1 = Victorian Doctors-in-Training agreement.

nodes.label: Establishment Calculator
nodes.rationale: Cover matrix x 7 = weekly demand; 17-22% leave/sick/study buffer converts floor FTE to establishment; deterministic arithmetic powering the director's business case and a buffer-health dial.

nodes.label: Medical Workforce Unit
nodes.rationale: The JMO buyer - bigger budget than any consultant group; recruitment angle: our ED lets you choose your shifts.

nodes.label: Open-Shift Marketplace
nodes.rationale: Cross-workforce offer/claim (admin-posted open shifts + staff give-aways) replacing the anyone-free-Saturday WhatsApp; CMO-claimed shifts avoid agency locum fees (measurable ROI); fast-follow because sync hardening removed the concurrent-writes blocker.

nodes.label: Relief Lines
nodes.rationale: 1-2 doctors/day rostered as relief absorb sickness first; escalation ladder: relief, under-hours juniors, CMO offer pool, locum, declared gap vs safe minimum.

nodes.label: Terms and Rotation Model
nodes.rationale: Term churn is structural (staggered 3-24-month terms never align with 8-week cycles): templates define stable lines, people occupy them for date ranges; changeover = occupant handover, not a re-roster; supersedes the part-cycle from/to roadmap item.

nodes.label: Adversarial Audit
nodes.rationale: 19 Aug: four independent audits over the finished branch - 20 findings fixed same day, 95/95 tests, 26 stored-XSS interpolations escaped, rollback dependency bug and sign-out cache leak closed; realtime isolation verified on staging.

nodes.label: Branding and Feature Flags
nodes.rationale: Per-org S.branding/S.features live as data in each org's blob - already synced and RLS-isolated, defaults reproduce the current look; includes per-org role noun and hospital-grouped picker.

nodes.label: Isolation Test
nodes.rationale: Hard gate: no second real org until Org A is provably denied Org B (12/12 probes both directions); proves RLS only - edge functions and realtime checked separately; re-run after any RLS change.

nodes.label: Multi-Org Edge Functions
nodes.rationale: Nearly missed: push-send trusted the org in the request body (cross-org push hole), ics was hard-wired to one org, notify functions read the allow-list unscoped; all four now org-scoped and fail-closed, must be redeployed with ORG/MYROSTA_ORG unset and CRON_SECRET set.

nodes.label: Multi-Tenant Foundation
nodes.rationale: One codebase serving many isolated orgs without a rewrite: auth, RLS allow-list, per-org blob and org-filtered realtime already exist, so the plan only adds an org dimension; onboarding = insert a row + invite an admin.

nodes.label: Org Resolution and Picker
nodes.rationale: resolveOrg() from my_orgs() at sign-in with a picker for multi-org users; falls back to single-org mode when my_orgs() is absent, so the app deploys before the SQL migration with zero behaviour change.

nodes.label: Org-Scoped Device Cache
nodes.rationale: A single shared cache key would merge one group's unsynced edits into another group's live roster for a legitimate dual-group member; orgKey() scopes cache, dirty flag and merge base per org.

nodes.label: Org-Scoped RLS Migration
nodes.rationale: Adds org to roster_members (default ed-default keeps existing rows working), (org,email) PK, org-scoped helpers, my_orgs(), orgs registry; never touches org_state contents, so rollback is policies-only. Never revert the composite PK on rollback.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Shift Times
nodes.rationale: Per-cycle shiftTimes via shiftTimesOf()/effShiftTimes(); defaults unchanged so zero behaviour change until edited. Done 7 Jul 2026.

nodes.label: Phase 2 Shift Types
nodes.rationale: Arbitrary shift types incl. rostered nights; do it while there is one org (no tenant migrations); the existing period field already carries the type id so data migrates untouched; ship with presets; designed JMO-ready so the junior module is configuration, not a rebuild.

nodes.label: Hospital Umbrella
nodes.rationale: Orgs carry a hospital grouping so a super-admin sees all their groups and the picker reads Site - Nurses / JMOs; cheap, makes five orgs feel like one product.

nodes.label: Roles as Zones
nodes.rationale: A slot is a labelled slot whether it names a room or a job; proven when nurse 2 was refused already-taken Triage while Staff nurse stayed bookable.

nodes.label: Scribe Shadow Roster
nodes.rationale: Scribes are paired to a consultant's shift, so their roster follows another org's booked slot; small build once the site's consultants are live.

nodes.label: Second Pilot Site
nodes.rationale: Five groups = five orgs under one hospital umbrella, not one shared roster (groups never share shifts, quotas or fairness); separate deployments rejected; site's confirmed 10:00-23:00 no-nights pattern puts all five groups on the existing engine in Stage 1, proven on staging 18 Aug.

nodes.label: MYROSTA Word Mark
nodes.rationale: Plain word mark first for broadest protection, classes 9 + 42; wording kept general (workforce scheduling, not medical) because healthcare-specific wording would narrow protection and might pull in class 44.

nodes.label: ROSTRA Prior Mark
nodes.rationale: ROSTRA reg. 730142 (automotive cruise-control electronics, class 9) is the mark to watch; Headstart exists to test whether an examiner would cite it despite the different goods.

nodes.label: TM Headstart
nodes.rationale: IP Australia pre-assessment route, converting to a full application; each class a separate fee.

nodes.label: Autonomy vs Automation Positioning
nodes.rationale: Lead with 'your staff pick their own shifts - the app keeps it fair': IRIS's AI-generates/admin-approves model cannot say that sentence.

nodes.label: Not-Build List
nodes.rationale: Closed doors: clinical companion (TGA exposure), payroll/award interpretation (graveyard), time-and-attendance, credentialing, generic all-industry rostering - protects healthcare-specialist positioning.

nodes.label: Optional-Module Principle
nodes.rationale: Every capability ships as an optional module any group can enable - never a hard-coded nurse or JMO feature; one engine, one product, configuration per group.

nodes.label: Deploy Order
nodes.rationale: APP then EDGE FUNCTIONS then SQL: the new app is provably inert on the old schema and functions carry fallbacks, while SQL-first would let old cached browsers issue unscoped member deletes stripping a person from every org.

nodes.label: Mustero Rejection
nodes.rationale: MUSTER is registered bare in classes 9/35 plus a cluster of software Muster marks, making Mustero a high deceptive-similarity risk; Myrosta vs ROSTRA (different word, different goods) is the stronger position.

nodes.label: Access Control
nodes.rationale: Sync allow-list from staff plus admins gates sign-in by email or mobile; idle auto-logout time for shared computers is set here.

nodes.label: Alt Email
nodes.rationale: A personal address for anyone whose hospital blocks external mail - they can sign in with either address.

nodes.label: Audit Log
nodes.rationale: Every approval and change is logged - nothing happens off the record; the log answers any query about a change.

nodes.label: Auto Draft
nodes.rationale: Drafts a fair, fully-covered roster to minimum cover in seconds, skipping anyone on leave - good practice is to auto-draft first, eyeball it, then release for self-roster.

nodes.label: Fixed Patterns
nodes.rationale: Weekly or fortnightly A/B patterns can be committed (locked); staff changes to a locked pattern require approval; a pattern day left as Any auto is placed by auto-draft in a balanced free zone around fixed-zone pins.

nodes.label: Locum Cover
nodes.rationale: A vacant cell can be assigned with a Locum tick - flagged with an L badge on the roster, a Locum tag in Daily, and Locum in the payroll export.

nodes.label: Make Admin
nodes.rationale: Only an existing admin can grant admin rights, and it is enforced by the database; syncing the allow-list never demotes an admin.

nodes.label: Non Clinical Mode
nodes.rationale: Coordinators and clerks who do not work clinical shifts stay off the roster but can still sign in and be made admins.

nodes.label: Payroll Export
nodes.rationale: One click exports every shift with correct times and leave pro-rated by EFT - no re-keying; a custom import template maps columns automatically and all export buttons are admin-only.

nodes.label: RosterOn Sheet
nodes.rationale: A two-sheet workbook: a readable roster grouped by Title matching RosterOn's cell format including overnight OC, plus a clean one-row-per-shift data sheet.

nodes.label: Staff Template
nodes.rationale: For departments with no spreadsheets: download, fill and upload the template and Myrosta builds the department.

nodes.label: Zones and Cover
nodes.rationale: Clinical areas with per-period headcounts plus a minimum and maximum cover floor and ceiling for each day.

nodes.label: Capacity Check
nodes.rationale: Directors enter needed cover, EFT and a realistic away-buffer to get a plain-words feasibility summary; what-ifs never touch the roster, every line of the maths is shown, and it prints a one-page business case.

nodes.label: Demo Sandbox
nodes.rationale: A /demo.html environment with sample data, safe to explore.

nodes.label: Fatigue Rules
nodes.rationale: Minimum rest between shifts (counting through the on-call end) and max consecutive clinical days, warning or blocking at booking time; off by default, per cycle, admin-overridable with a warning.

nodes.label: Per Cycle Shift Times
nodes.rationale: AM/PM/on-call/CST start and end times are per-cycle settings; booking labels, payroll and RosterOn exports, calendar files, hours and fatigue maths all follow them.

nodes.label: ED Pilot Ask
nodes.rationale: The video closes by asking for a single eight-week pilot in the ED - low cost, low risk.

nodes.label: Offer to Group
nodes.rationale: A consultant offers one of their own upcoming shifts back to the group; a colleague's claim transfers the shift automatically.

nodes.label: Open Shift Marketplace
nodes.rationale: Admin broadcasts post-publication gaps and staff can hand shifts back to the group; claims are first-come or admin-approved, pass the same guards as any booking (leave, double-booking, zone, fatigue, quota with optional confirmed over-quota gap fill), are race-safe and audit-logged; fixed shifts cannot be given away and entries auto-expire the day after the shift.

nodes.label: Home Screen Install
nodes.rationale: Adding the web app to the home screen makes it open full-screen like a native app with nothing to install from a store.

nodes.label: Myrosta
nodes.rationale: Defined here as the Emergency Department roster app: your shifts, fair self-rostering, leave and swaps on any device.

nodes.label: Send Feedback
nodes.rationale: Help tab feedback goes straight to the roster admin - a bug, an idea, or something confusing.

nodes.label: Option A Open Booking
nodes.rationale: Today's system - book your exact day, period and zone instantly, first in wins contested slots; won the vote so it was kept.

nodes.label: Option B Turn Based
nodes.rationale: Everyone picks in a rotating order that reverses each round.

nodes.label: Option C Preference Week Draw
nodes.rationale: Runner-up and the named plan-B - fully specified in its own explainer, to be built only if the race complaint returns against the Q1 mandate-meter baseline.

nodes.label: Option D Points Budget
nodes.rationale: Points follow your hours, weighted onto the days that matter most, with losing bids refunded; design-complete but not built.

nodes.label: Option E Drafted for You
nodes.rationale: Mark preferences once and the system builds the whole roster with a visible reason for every allocation; an E-lite exists as auto-draft plus adjust.

nodes.label: Calendar Export
nodes.rationale: One tap pushes shifts with reminders into Apple, Google, Outlook or Teams calendars as a .ics file.

nodes.label: Leave Planner
nodes.rationale: A colour-coded whole-year view of team leave so staff can plan requests likely to be approved.

nodes.label: Myrosta
nodes.rationale: Replaces the manual roster spreadsheet with a web app: each consultant sees their own shifts, the group self-rosters fairly, leave and swaps are handled with context, and shifts export straight to payroll; data hosted in Australia and syncing live across devices.

nodes.label: Shared Computer Mode
nodes.rationale: A session flagged as shared never persists and auto-signs-out after idle - ward computers stay safe while personal phones stay signed in.

nodes.label: Shift Quota
nodes.rationale: Counted per fortnight by default to match pay; uneven remainders can be placed by staff in whichever fortnight suits.

nodes.label: Unplanned Leave
nodes.rationale: Approving UPL clears the booked shift so the gap is visible for a colleague to pick up as locum cover.

nodes.label: Demo Video Script
nodes.rationale: A 3-4 minute benefit-led screen recording to win buy-in, with per-audience emphasis: staff on fairness and shifts-on-your-phone, admins on auto-draft and context approvals, directors on transparency, governance and near-zero cost.

nodes.label: Director Onboarding Email
nodes.rationale: Post-walkthrough email; the director's mobile/email must be added to the access list first, with IG-and-IT summary and user guide attached for governance.

nodes.label: Go Live Announcement
nodes.rationale: Announces to the ED consultant group that the roster has moved off the spreadsheet, with sign-in steps and the first self-roster round date; includes an ultra-short chat version.

nodes.label: Invite Note
nodes.rationale: Paste-ready onboarding note for the ED team covering SMS-first sign-in, home-screen install, a QR handout, and code-troubleshooting.

nodes.label: Pilot Emails
nodes.rationale: Launch and reminder emails for the next-cycle pilot, stressing that the app was built by one of the team and changes based on feedback.

nodes.label: Pilot Feedback Survey
nodes.rationale: A 2-minute questionnaire whose answers decide what is kept and what changes - ease of use, sign-in, seeing shifts, fairness of self-rostering, comparison with the old spreadsheet, and willingness to keep using it.

nodes.label: Round 1 Survey
nodes.rationale: Anonymous vote on how to run self-rostering, with no demographic questions because they would de-anonymise a group this size; top-two first-choice votes advance and second choices only break ties. Outcome 5 Aug 2026: Option A won, Option C runner-up - no Round 2, no change made, and results were fed back to close the loop.

nodes.label: Training Video Script
nodes.rationale: A 5-6 minute how-to for the whole team - product intro, staff how-to, then admin how-to - narrated with AI voiceover via CapCut, ElevenLabs or Descript so no video skills are needed.

nodes.label: Approval Context
nodes.rationale: Shows EFT, leave already taken, who else is away and the daily cap so approvals are decided with context; a decision auto-updates roster and leave planner, notifies the person and drafts the confirmation email.

nodes.label: Per Cycle Settings
nodes.rationale: Cover, zones, method and quotas apply to the selected cycle only, so changing the next roster never alters a published one; Prepare next cycle copies the current setup as a starting point.

nodes.label: Parallel Run Pilot
nodes.rationale: The existing system stays the official roster for the 3 Aug - 27 Sep 2026 cycle while staff also self-roster in Myrosta - a no-risk trial purely for experience and feedback; if the two ever differ, the official roster wins.

nodes.label: Compare and Swap Booking
nodes.rationale: Each booking is an atomic compare-and-swap: if the shared record changed since load, the app reloads, re-checks capacity and replays the pick, so simultaneous claims cannot double-book; admin edits use last-write-wins with realtime refresh - fine for a small ED group.

nodes.label: Sydney Data Residency
nodes.rationale: Region ap-southeast-2 keeps Australian staff data onshore, aligned with the Privacy Act 1988 and the APPs.

nodes.label: Collision Proof Booking
nodes.rationale: Only free slots are shown and a taken slot disappears for everyone instantly, so two people can never book the same shift.

nodes.label: Self Roster Methods
nodes.rationale: Cohort waves, snake-draft rotating turns, guarded free-for-all, and auto-draft plus adjust - admin-selectable per cycle so fairness rules and quotas mean the last person to log in still gets a fair go.

nodes.label: Book Shifts and Request Leave or Swaps
nodes.norm_label: book shifts and request leave or swaps

nodes.label: View Shifts in List or Calendar
nodes.norm_label: view shifts in list or calendar

nodes.label: index.html
nodes.rationale: The whole app is one self-contained file running entirely in the browser (localStorage), so no server is needed to use it and hosting is a drag-and-drop.

nodes.label: Load Save Data Layer
nodes.rationale: The two functions load() and save() are the single choke point for all reads and writes - the design decision that made swapping localStorage for Supabase a contained change.

nodes.label: notify-rounds Function
nodes.rationale: Runs every 5 minutes by cron, independent of the in-app flip; server-side flags mark each message sent once, and a compare-and-swap write ensures it never clobbers a booking made at the same moment.

nodes.label: notify-shifts Function
nodes.rationale: Daily you-are-on-tomorrow reminders to each person's personal email or mobile, skipping anyone off or on leave and noting locum shifts; cron is UTC and does not follow daylight saving, so the hour needs nudging for exactness year-round.

nodes.label: push-send Function
nodes.rationale: The legacy JWT gateway check is turned off because it rejects genuine new-key sign-in tokens; the function verifies the caller's token server-side and matches them against the allow-list itself, and payloads carry only what the bell shows - no phone numbers or payroll data.

nodes.label: ics Edge Function
nodes.rationale: JWT verification must be off because calendar apps fetch with no login headers - the secret token in the URL is the credential; only open, closed or published cycles are returned so drafts never leak, and invalid tokens get a bare 404.

nodes.label: CLOUD Config
nodes.rationale: url, key, org, adminEmails and allowedDomains bootstrap the app; adminEmails remains the bootstrap so admins cannot be locked out; allowedDomains is a friendly first gate while the allow-list plus RLS is the real enforcement; different org values run separate rosters from one database.

nodes.label: org_state Table
nodes.rationale: The entire app state is one JSONB row keyed by org - simple and matching the app's single-document model; the trade-off is that fine-grained admin-vs-staff rules stay app-side, with per-record tables as the known upgrade path.

nodes.label: RLS Policies
nodes.rationale: SECURITY DEFINER helpers is_member and is_admin_member check the allow-list without recursion; DELETE on org_state was revoked after the 5 Jul 2026 council review because the app never issues it.

nodes.label: roster_members Table
nodes.rationale: The allow-list: only emails or phones on this table can read or write anything even with a valid login; members can read the list, only admins can change it, and a seeded admin bootstraps access.

nodes.label: Import Data
nodes.rationale: Reads existing roster, leave planner and EFT spreadsheets as-is, pulling in EFT, hours and employee numbers - no re-keying to adopt the app.

nodes.label: Round Scheduling
nodes.rationale: Schedule open and close date-times auto-open and auto-close the round with a countdown banner and in-app notifications; email/SMS reminders are an optional server add-on.

nodes.label: Equity Tab
nodes.rationale: Shows tough-shift share versus team average (weekends, Mon/Fri PM, on-call, public holidays, locum) so everyone can see who is carrying the tough shifts; admins choose what counts as tough.

nodes.label: Multiorg Foundation
nodes.rationale: One hospital, many staff groups - every data path, the allow-list and the server functions org-scoped, with per-group branding and feature flags; falls back to single-group behaviour until the database migration runs.

nodes.label: Public Holiday Marking
nodes.rationale: Admins mark a PH from the roster day header or Daily toggle; the badge shows everywhere so staff see it at booking time.

nodes.label: Request Conversations
nodes.rationale: Admins can ask a question instead of declining; the private thread stays on the request, closed and kept once decided, and swap partners can join.

nodes.label: Hospital Intranet Hosting
nodes.rationale: Best for governance - data stays inside the hospital network; recommended for real staff data over public hosting.

nodes.label: Netlify
nodes.rationale: Free static hosting; the drop page gives an instant shareable URL and a free account makes it permanent.

nodes.label: Phase A Hosting
nodes.rationale: Static hosting with per-device data - good for a director demo or single-admin use; public Phase A links have no login so only demo or anonymised data belongs there.

nodes.label: Phase B Multi User
nodes.rationale: Browsers cannot share localStorage, so true multi-user needs a shared database plus login; because all reads and writes already go through load() and save(), wiring the backend was a contained change.

nodes.label: Custom Domain
nodes.rationale: myrosta.com.au is registered under the founder's ABN; order matters - DNS and HTTPS live first, then update the Supabase URLs, then test sign-in, otherwise the login will not land on the right address.

nodes.label: Path A Demo Link
nodes.rationale: A 5-minute no-backend, no-login public link for the director demo; data stays per-device so only demo or representative data is used.

nodes.label: Path B Multi User
nodes.rationale: The 30-minute full setup: Supabase project in Sydney, SQL schema with a re-seeded admin email, keys into the CLOUD config, hosting, Supabase URL configuration, custom SMTP with the Token template, then allow-list sync and staff invites.

nodes.label: Twilio Messaging
nodes.rationale: Twilio Verify (used for OTP) cannot send reminders; SMS reminders need a Messaging sender, which for Australia must be registered - so email reminders ship immediately and SMS is added later.

nodes.label: Phone Push
nodes.rationale: Web Push chosen over a native app because the PWA path covers it; iPhone needs iOS 16.4+ with Home Screen install; the in-app bell keeps working regardless - push is an extra per-phone layer with an unread badge where supported.

nodes.label: VAPID Keys
nodes.rationale: The private key exists only in the function's secrets and a private Desktop file - not in the app or repo - so a visible push endpoint is useless to anyone else; expired subscriptions self-heal and are not pruned server-side because that would need a CAS write-back not worth it at pilot scale.

nodes.label: Calendar Token
nodes.rationale: The link is the password: it exposes one person's shifts only (no contact or payroll data); reset kills a leaked URL instantly and is audit-logged; tokens live inside shared roster data - acceptable because colleagues already see the whole roster - and should move to their own table at multi-org time.

nodes.label: Live Calendar Feed
nodes.rationale: Staff subscribe once via a personal secret webcal link and roster changes flow into phone calendars automatically; the manual .ics download stays as the instant-snapshot fallback with the same event IDs so the two sources stay consistent.

nodes.label: OTP Email Setup
nodes.rationale: Custom SMTP must be connected first because Supabase locks template editing and rate-limits built-in email; the template must include the Token variable or the email only shows a magic link instead of the 6-digit code.

nodes.label: Realtime Sync
nodes.rationale: The app loads state on open, saves back debounced, and subscribes to realtime so remote changes refresh automatically - a booking on one device updates everyone.

nodes.label: Resend
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the easiest free SMTP service for sign-in codes, sending as noreply@myrosta.com.au; connecting it unlocks template editing and removes the built-in rate limit.

nodes.label: Google OAuth
nodes.rationale: Optional provider, e.g. as a personal fallback, following the same pattern as Entra ID.

nodes.label: Microsoft Entra ID
nodes.rationale: The provider hospitals ask for; hospital IT does a standard app registration and Supabase holds the client ID, secret and tenant URL.

nodes.label: Single Sign On
nodes.rationale: Built and dormant behind CLOUD flags; SSO never bypasses the allow-list - the provider's verified work email runs the exact same roster_members check as OTP; sessions and shared-computer mode behave identically, and rollback is flipping the flag back.

nodes.label: Supabase
nodes.rationale: Hosted database with built-in auth and realtime on a free tier - no server to manage; filling three CLOUD values switches the whole app from local to shared cloud data, and blanking them switches it back.

nodes.label: Twilio Verify
nodes.rationale: Chosen for Australian SMS sign-in because Verify provisions Twilio's own AU-approved sender - an unregistered alphanumeric sender ID fails with Twilio error 21703 and registration takes days; a branded sender is a later nice-to-have.

nodes.label: Passwordless Sign In
nodes.rationale: A 6-digit code by SMS or email with persistent per-device sessions makes login effectively one-time - no password to remember; SMS is the default because hospital mailboxes often block external email.

nodes.label: Phase 2 Reminders
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 flips rounds open/closed in-app; Phase 2 adds automatic email (and optional SMS) reminders when a round opens, 24 hours before close, and at close.

nodes.label: Marketplace Push Guide
nodes.rationale: Two features shipped together in Aug 2026, both off by default until the admin switches them on; the marketplace needs no server setup, push needs one function and two secrets.

nodes.label: Sync Hardening
nodes.rationale: Council-review outcome: concurrent edits from multiple users merge safely so requests, approvals, messages and bookings cannot be lost or resurrected; offline changes recover on next sign-in with an honest will-sync-when-online status.

nodes.label: Information Governance
nodes.rationale: Roster data includes mobile numbers and leave - personal information - so it must sit behind a login and the hospital's information-governance and IT security rules must be checked first.

nodes.label: Locum Cover and Unplanned Leave (UPL)
nodes.rationale: A sick consultant logs UPL; approving it clears the booked shift leaving a visible gap a colleague can pick up. Ticking Locum cover on the vacant cell flags the shift with a pink L badge on the roster, a Locum tag in Daily, and Locum in the payroll export - so cover on top of the normal roster is visibly counted and paid.

nodes.label: Payroll Export (RosterOn)
nodes.rationale: One-click export of every shift with correct times (AM, PM, on-call, CST) and leave pro-rated by EFT eliminates re-keying into payroll; uploading the hospital's RosterOn import template maps columns automatically with a chosen date format; a RosterOn sheet button builds a readable Title-grouped roster plus a one-row-per-shift data sheet. All export buttons are admin-only.

nodes.label: Zones (Clinical Areas)
nodes.rationale: Admin-defined clinical areas with per-period staffing needs, minimum and maximum daily cover, and an extra-slot unlock order (AM and PM together, AM first, or PM first) - extra slots open only once minimum cover is filled. Configured per cycle so changes never alter a published roster.

nodes.label: Collision-proof Live Booking
nodes.rationale: Bookings only count once saved to the cloud, so simultaneous taps are resolved and only one sticks - double-booking is impossible, losing signal never half-books, and a taken slot disappears for everyone else in real time.

nodes.label: Access Allow-list with Row-Level Security
nodes.rationale: Authorisation is an allow-list of approved emails and mobiles enforced by database row-level security, so even a valid login from an unlisted address is denied with a No access screen; admin rights can only be granted by an existing admin and are enforced by the database. Known limitation flagged for sign-off: fine-grained staff-edit-own-entries rules are enforced in the app, not the database (roster stored as one document); a per-record design is the planned enhancement if higher assurance is needed.

nodes.label: Audit Log
nodes.rationale: Logs every approval and change so nothing happens off the record - the admin's answer when anyone queries a change, and the direct fix for the old Excel roster's lack of any who-edited-what-and-when trail.

nodes.label: Australian Data Residency (Sydney)
nodes.rationale: Roster data is kept in a single record in a Supabase PostgreSQL database provisioned in Sydney (ap-southeast-2) so staff data stays onshore, aligned with the Privacy Act 1988 and APPs; the only cross-border flow is a transient sign-in code with an email or phone number via Twilio and Resend, switchable to hospital SMTP to keep email onshore if required. HTTPS everywhere and encryption at rest.

nodes.label: Myrosta
nodes.rationale: Bespoke in-house web app built by an ED consultant to replace a manually maintained 56-column Excel roster: one place to see your own shifts, self-roster fairly, request leave and swaps, and export straight to payroll. A single self-contained HTML/JavaScript page with a local mode (browser-only) and a shared mode (hosted database, live sync, individual logins). Holds no patient or clinical data by design; processes staff personal information only and is intended to comply with the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) and the APPs.

nodes.label: Passwordless 6-Digit Code Sign-in
nodes.rationale: No passwords by design: a one-time 6-digit code by SMS (Twilio Verify) or email (Resend), then sessions persist per device - effectively a single sign-in with no passwords stored. Codes carry only the number and the recipient's address, never roster data; the SMS path and an optional personal Alt email deliberately work around hospital mail servers that block external email.

nodes.label: Shared Computer Mode
nodes.rationale: Ward and shared computers get a this-is-a-shared-computer tick at sign-in: the session lives in session-only storage cleared when the browser closes and auto-logs-out after an admin-set idle timeout, while personal devices stay signed in - balancing one-tap convenience with shared-terminal safety.

nodes.label: Parallel-Run Pilot (Aug-Sep 2026)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately zero-risk adoption: the existing system remains the official roster for shifts and pay while staff also self-roster in Myrosta for the 3 August - 27 September 2026 cycle (round opens 29 June) purely for the experience and feedback; on any discrepancy the official roster wins. Framed as made by one of us and shaped by feedback, to earn trust before any switch.

nodes.label: Fixed Patterns
nodes.rationale: Weekly or fortnightly A/B set patterns can be committed (locked) so staff edits route to the admin for approval instead of changing silently; a fixed-pattern day can set the period and leave the zone as Any (auto) for auto-draft to place in a balanced free zone around fixed-zone pins, flagging clashes.

nodes.label: Leave Planner
nodes.rationale: Colour-coded year view of the whole team's leave so staff can pick quieter days likelier to be approved, and admins can see who else is away and the daily cap before deciding a request.

nodes.label: Self-roster Methods
nodes.rationale: Four configurable round styles - cohort waves, snake-draft (rotating turns), guarded free-for-all, and auto-draft + adjust - all tracking everyone against quota and caps so shifts spread evenly and login order does not decide fair shares. Rounds can be scheduled to auto-open and auto-close with a countdown and notifications.

nodes.label: Shift Quota (Per Fortnight)
nodes.rationale: Each person's EFT-based shift quota is counted per fortnight by default deliberately to match pay periods; a Staff-choose setting lets a consultant whose quota does not divide evenly place the extra shift in whichever fortnight suits, still capped at their total. Quotas are per-cycle and are the fairness backstop in every rostering method.

nodes.label: Admin Pain Points
nodes.rationale: Demo framing of why admins need Myrosta: drafting each cycle roster by hand, complex Excel formulas, maintaining fairness, maintaining tallies and departmental cover, no backup against Excel failure, no auto-update, and no audit log of who edited what and when.

nodes.label: Staff Pain Points
nodes.rationale: Demo framing of why staff need Myrosta: Teams login hoops, hunting a 56-grid Excel sheet, no quick view of the daily roster or their own shifts, no calendar export, no leave or swap requests, and multiple interfaces to coordinate and schedule.

nodes.label: Two-Round Vote and One-Cycle Trial
nodes.rationale: Change process designed for legitimacy: anonymous two-round Microsoft Forms vote, one response per person - round 1 picks the top two options, round 2 is a head-to-head. The winner runs ONE roster cycle as an explicit trial, reviewed against staff sentiment plus an equity summary of how weekends, evenings and on-call actually fell; revert if it does not earn its place - nothing is permanent. Guarantee stated up front: no option changes quotas, coverage minimums or safe-hours rules, and none carries a cost.

nodes.label: Option A - Open Booking (First Tap Wins)
nodes.norm_label: option a - open booking (first tap wins)
nodes.rationale: Kept on the ballot as the status quo: instant certainty (first tap holds the slot), nothing new to learn, roster fills fast. Trade-offs: speed alone decides contested slots; staff post-nights, on leave or busy at opening pick from leftovers; no memory, so the same quick people win every cycle with no compensation. Its weakness is exactly the race complaint that triggered the fairness review.

nodes.label: Option B - Turn-based Booking (Rotating Order)
nodes.rationale: Rotating published order kills the opening sprint and is explainable in one line; rotation is the fairness engine - everyone passes through both front and back of the queue across cycles, with a reversing snake variant per round. Trade-offs: elapsed time (12 people x 24h windows is nearly two weeks); losing still happens within a cycle since rotation compensates only across cycles; a turn can land badly on leave or clinical days; the process needs chasing when turns stall. Flagged by the author as an immediate stopgap because it needs nothing new.

nodes.label: Audited Draw Receipts
nodes.rationale: Every placement carries its reason - uncontested grants, priority wins, seeded re-checkable draws, auto-fills, rare prefer-not use, zone steering - in an append-only log visible to all, so nobody has to trust the process: anyone can look, and the answer to why didn't I get the 15th is the same record a month later.

nodes.label: Fixed-First Roster Layering
nodes.rationale: Fixed patterns are stamped first so nothing changes for fixed-pattern colleagues - their trade-off (certainty instead of choice) was settled when the pattern was agreed. Flexible staff contest only the remaining capacity, fully-filled days show as full so nobody wastes a mark or enters a draw for a slot that does not exist, and priority points are deliberately a flexible-staff-only ledger while the equity view still counts everyone's tough shifts. A fixed colleague's leave returns slots to the pool; hybrids go through preference week for their flexible remainder. Every option A-E keeps this layering.

nodes.label: Option C - Preference Week + Fair Draw
nodes.norm_label: option c - preference week + fair draw
nodes.rationale: Designed to remove both the race and the feeling of one: a sealed 7-day preference window where timing is irrelevant; uncontested picks are simply granted, contested slots go first to priority points then to an audited seeded draw; draw losers gain a carry-over point so the system self-corrects (it owes you next time, automatically and visibly). Every allocation carries a one-line receipt. Trade-offs: results arrive at the deadline rather than instantly; contested losers visibly miss the day they wanted (but gain priority); a small new habit to learn; modest setup needed. Recommended by the Director Brief as the best fit for the group.

nodes.label: Priority Points Carry-over
nodes.rationale: Designed as the system's memory so luck evens out: lose a draw and you gain +1 point usable from the very next contested draw; points never expire and carry across cycles; they reset only when they have done their job (winning a contested slot); uncontested slots never touch them. By construction whoever has the worst luck this cycle is first in line next time - equity without negotiation.

nodes.label: UA Cannot-Work Budget
nodes.rationale: UA days are capped (about one per three shifts owed, rounded up, minimum 6, auto-adjusted for leave) precisely so an accepted UA can be guaranteed never overridden by draw or auto-fill. A zone-aware coverage floor stops a day accepting UA once the eligible pool would drop to minimum staffing plus a margin; oversubscribed UA is decided by draw and carry-over at window close, never by who marked first. Unlimited free prefer-not marks exist so UA is saved for genuine cannots, and leave is kept separate so it never consumes the budget.

nodes.label: Zone Profiles and Constrained-First Placement
nodes.rationale: The ballot deliberately stays about days - nobody marks zones. Admin-set profiles (eligible zones, percentage targets) drive zone-by-zone capacity underneath; most-constrained staff are placed first, dissolving most clashes without a draw; percentage targets balance across the cycle rather than day by day; auto-fill respects eligibility and flags impossible cover to the admin; a scarce-skill guardrail warns before the last cover for a zone goes unavailable, and draw records show zone scope so nobody wonders why a colleague was not in the draw.

nodes.label: Option D - Points Budget (Bidding)
nodes.rationale: Sealed bidding lets staff say HOW MUCH a day matters, not just that it matters - a family event can outrank a mild preference. Budget scales with contracted hours (about 1 point per rosterable hour: 76 full-time, 56 at 0.7 EFT) so every EFT holds equal power per shift owed; losing bids are refunded in full; unspent points carry over capped at about 1.5x a cycle budget to prevent hoarding. Runs on the same engine as Option C (sealed week, audited draws, carry-over priority for ties); spending nothing makes it behave exactly like C. Trade-offs: colleagues bid against each other for personal events, it rewards tactical play, losing a heavy bid stings, and it is the hardest option to explain and run. The author's close second choice.

nodes.label: Option E - Preferences In, Roster Out (Drafted)
nodes.norm_label: option e - preferences in, roster out (drafted)
nodes.rationale: Asks the least effort: mark days once (same UA budget and prefer-not marks as Option C, plus standing preferences like cluster or spread) and an engine drafts the whole roster in one pass. Hard rules (UA, leave, staffing, safe-hours) are walls, never broken; contested days are decided by two observable facts - who missed the most marked days recently (the same carry-over idea as Option C) and who carries the higher tough-shift share - with losers' ledgers credited so compensation is built in. No race, no draws, nobody visibly loses a head-to-head, and the good-and-bad spread is balanced by design. Trade-offs: you receive a roster rather than choose it, single allocations are harder to explain, least sense of personal control - the computer chose takes trust; a larger undertaking to build.

nodes.label: Director Recommendation of Option C
nodes.rationale: Option C recommended because it removes the race and the feeling of one, everyone still chooses their own days, it is explainable in one breath, and it self-corrects - whoever misses a contested day holds priority for the next. Option D is the close second: same engine as C plus weighting for the days that matter most, right only if the group wants that control and accepts the strategy it demands. Option B is the immediate stopgap needing nothing new. Setup cost acknowledged: A and B need nothing new, C modest setup, D and E larger undertakings.

nodes.label: Self-roster Race Problem
nodes.rationale: Staff complaint that the self-roster round feels like a race: whoever logs in first gets their preferred shifts, while anyone on leave or flat-out clinically at opening picks from what is left. Judged a fair call deserving a group decision rather than a change imposed from above - the trigger for the five-option fairness review and vote.
